page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this arm64 server features 64 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution and 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. The CPU architecture includes a 32 MB L3 cache and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, though it lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX or AMX. Local storage is absent, requiring network-attached storage, but the instance is equipped with a high-speed 100 Gbps baseline network interface managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The c6gn.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and software compilation tasks. It also excels in memory bandwidth for small cached blocks and registers high throughput for static web serving and Redis SET operations. However, single-core execution is a notable tradeoff; both Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the lower percentiles. Large-block memory bandwidth and LLM inference speeds for medium-to-large models remain in the average to weak ranges.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton architecture offers high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance per unit of power compared to traditional x86 architectures. This makes the instance highly suitable for scale-out, multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the 64 dedicated cores and 100 Gbps network bandwidth. Recommended workloads include high-throughput web serving, distributed caching, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. It is less suited for single-threaded applications or memory-intensive databases requiring high RAM-to-CPU ratios.
